description: Systems engineering methodology decomposed. Requirements analysis (functional, performance, interface, constraints), architecture (logical + physical), trade studies, V&V planning, technical reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR), risk management, configuration management, INCOSE practices.

sub_mechanisms.name: functional_requirements
sub_mechanisms.definition: What the system must do. Behaviour, not implementation.
sub_mechanisms.why: Distinct from how. 'System shall navigate to destination' vs 'using GPS'. Implementation chosen during design.

sub_mechanisms.name: performance_requirements
sub_mechanisms.definition: How well. Latency, throughput, accuracy, availability. Quantified.
sub_mechanisms.why: Measurable. Drives architecture decisions. SHALL + numeric value + units + condition.

sub_mechanisms.name: interface_requirements
sub_mechanisms.definition: Boundaries between components. Inputs, outputs, protocols, voltages.
sub_mechanisms.why: Decouple. Each component developed against its interfaces. ICDs (Interface Control Documents) formalise.

sub_mechanisms.name: constraint_requirements
sub_mechanisms.definition: Imposed limits: cost, weight, regulations, materials, environment.
sub_mechanisms.why: Bound solution space. Often externally imposed. Mass < X kg. Compliance with regulation Y.

sub_mechanisms.name: logical_vs_physical_architecture
sub_mechanisms.definition: Logical: functions + flows. Physical: components allocated to functions.
sub_mechanisms.why: Separation enables design exploration. Many physical mappings possible from one logical. Trade studies pick.

sub_mechanisms.name: trade_study_weighted_decision
sub_mechanisms.definition: Criteria + weights + alternatives + scores. Weighted sum identifies winner.
sub_mechanisms.why: Document rationale. Subjective but structured. Pugh matrix common. Pareto when multiple objectives.

sub_mechanisms.name: verification_vs_validation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Verification: built right (meets spec). Validation: right thing (meets needs).
sub_mechanisms.why: Different questions. V: tests against requirements. V: tests against stakeholder needs. Both required.

sub_mechanisms.name: technical_reviews_SRR_PDR_CDR
sub_mechanisms.definition: Systems Requirements Review → Preliminary Design Review → Critical Design Review. Gates.
sub_mechanisms.why: Stop bad designs early. Each: complete artifact, panel review. Standard NASA + DoD process.

sub_mechanisms.name: risk_register_matrix
sub_mechanisms.definition: List risks; assess likelihood × impact. Color-coded matrix.
sub_mechanisms.why: Ongoing risk management. Reviewed at reviews. Mitigations tracked. Standard PM + SE practice.

sub_mechanisms.name: configuration_management
sub_mechanisms.definition: Track + control changes to baseline. Configuration Control Board approves.
sub_mechanisms.why: Many engineers, many components. Versions matter. CM tools (git, doors, PLM). Standard SE.

sub_mechanisms.name: MBSE_model_based
sub_mechanisms.definition: Model-Based Systems Engineering. SysML diagrams replace text documents.
sub_mechanisms.why: Modern direction. Single source of truth model. Tools: MagicDraw, Cameo, SystemWeaver. Industry-wide adoption growing.

sub_mechanisms.name: INCOSE_handbook
sub_mechanisms.definition: International Council on Systems Engineering. Body of knowledge + best practices.
sub_mechanisms.why: Standard reference. CSEP certification. Standard methodology basis.

derivation_rules.name: requirements_drive_architecture
derivation_rules.why: Without requirements: no basis for comparison. With: trade study scores each architecture. Foundation of SE process.

derivation_rules.name: V_validates_against_needs_not_spec
if: product meets specification but not user need
derivation_rules.why: Spec might be wrong. Validation tests against need. Verification against spec. Both needed. Common failure: V&V conflated.

derivation_rules.name: trade_studies_document_rationale
derivation_rules.why: Without: future engineers don't know why. With: decisions auditable + revisitable. Standard at major decision points.

derivation_rules.name: design_reviews_catch_issues_early
then: fix costs orders of magnitude less than later
derivation_rules.why: Rule of 10: each phase is 10× more expensive to fix than previous. Design review catches at design (cheapest). Standard NASA/DoD.

derivation_rules.name: MBSE_eliminates_documentation_drift
if: system modeled in SysML with tooling
derivation_rules.why: Text docs drift. Model: single source. Changes propagate. Cost: tooling complexity, learning curve. Industry direction.
